title: Start your first session — two directions

steps.path: The first screen after setup finishes (shown in Midnight, the theme a new install starts in; switch to Light at the top right)
steps.headline: Which first 'Start your first session' screen?

variants.label: Today
variants.summary: Small form: folder, model, Skip permissions switch, Cancel and a 'Create session' button that wraps onto two lines.

variants.label: D1 · Roomy form
variants.summary: Bigger Outfit heading, a wider form so nothing wraps, no Cancel (there is nothing to go back to on the first screen), one full-width 'Start session' button.
variants.risk: Still asks about folder, model and Skip permissions before the user has seen anything.

variants.label: D2 · One button
variants.summary: One big 'Start your first session' button using the folder and model setup already chose; 'Change folder or model' under it opens the D1 form.
variants.risk: A first-timer may not notice which folder the assistant will work in; it's named in the line under the button.

steps.path: The theme the app opens in right after setup
steps.headline: Which theme should a brand-new install open in, after the lavender setup?
steps.today: Setup is brand lavender. The moment it finishes, the app switches to Midnight, a near-black theme, because that's the default for new installs.
steps.problem: Going from bright lavender straight to near-black is the sharpest jump in the whole first-run, and it happens on the first screen of the real app.

options.label: Follow light or dark
options.summary: Light if the computer is in light mode, Midnight if it's in dark mode.
pros: Matches the rest of the person's computer from the first minute.
Light users get a gentle step from lavender.
cons: Dark-mode users still get the lavender-to-dark jump.

options.label: Always Light
pros: The smallest jump from setup for everyone.
cons: Bright for someone who keeps everything dark.

options.label: Keep Midnight
pros: No change; it's the look the app is known for.
